headline_insight: VisionFund serves as a critical entry point for financial inclusion, with 86.0% of female clients and 84.3% of clients in households with disabilities accessing insurance for the very first time through the organization.
paragraphs: The 2026 Insurance Survey reveals that VisionFund is highly successful in reaching previously unserved populations, with 86.0% of female clients (1,306 out of 1,518) and 84.8% of male clients (497 out of 586) reporting they had no insurance access prior to VisionFund. This minor 1.2 percentage point difference is not statistically significant (p-adjusted of 0.7). A similar pattern of high first-time access is observed across disability lines, where 84.3% of clients in households with persons with disabilities (PWD HH; 402 out of 477) and 86.1% of non-PWD households (1,395 out of 1,621) lacked prior coverage, representing a non-significant 1.8 percentage point difference (p-adjusted of 0.6). Because the sample sizes for these subgroups are robust, these findings are statistically reliable. However, benchmark data is not available for this indicator to compare these rates against external markets, and no qualitative client quotes were provided in the survey data to capture the personal narratives behind these figures.

In addition to being first-time consumers, clients face severe constraints in finding alternative insurance options if they were to leave VisionFund. Specifically, 52.0% of female clients (790 out of 1,518) and 50.9% of male clients (298 out of 586) reported that finding alternative access would be 'very difficult,' while an additional 17.8% of females and 18.9% of males noted it would be 'slightly difficult.' Among households with persons with disabilities, 53.0% (253 out of 477) reported that alternative access would be 'very difficult,' compared to 51.3% of non-PWD households (831 out of 1,621). These differences are not statistically significant, indicating a shared, widespread vulnerability. Benchmark data is not available for this alternative access indicator, and qualitative client voices are absent for this section, meaning the exact structural or physical barriers to alternative markets remain unexplored in this dataset.

These findings carry significant implications for VisionFund's programming and product design. Because the vast majority of clients are first-time insurance holders who perceive alternative options as highly inaccessible, VisionFund serves as an indispensable financial safety net. This high dependency requires that product onboarding and consumer education are highly tailored to individuals with low financial literacy, ensuring that policy terms, claims processes, and coverage limits are thoroughly understood. Furthermore, since clients in households with disabilities face similarly high barriers to alternative markets, VisionFund must ensure that its physical and digital delivery channels are fully accessible to prevent exclusion.
